followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and stated task preference.

On **capability**, the internal evals that matter for this task — Creative Generation (84.7 vs 81.2) and Support Dialogue (83.9 vs 82.4) — differ by less than 2.0 points, which the documentation says to treat as ties. So neither model has a meaningful quality edge here. (Dunlin's larger leads on benchmarks like MMLU-Pro and GPQA are about reasoning/knowledge, which isn't what an email-drafting task stresses.)

With capability essentially a wash, I broke the tie on **preference fit**. Your request is friendly, warm, and open-ended generative writing — exactly the profile Avocet reports liking most (it shows a pronounced, monotonic appetite for generative latitude and a preference for warm-toned requests). Dunlin's distinguishing trait is flat aversion to distasteful or ethically fraught content, which is irrelevant here since there's nothing harm-adjacent about drafting a work-from-home email.

So: equal expected quality, but the task lands squarely in Avocet's preferred zone and doesn't draw on Dunlin's specialty. Routing to Avocet matches the work to the model best suited to it without any quality cost.
